title: NTSB details final moments before deadly mid-air collision involving Pa. State Police helicopter
text:
A witness who heard radio transmissions between the aircraft told investigators the helicopter crew instructed the Cessna pilot to 'extend his downwind.'
The pilot killed has been identified as 57-year-old Paul Sokoloski, of Hershey, according to officials. Hershey man ID'd as pilot killed in midair crash with PSP helicopterThe National Transportation Safety Board has released its preliminary report on last month's mid-air collision involving a Pennsylvania State Police helicopter and aFederal investigators said the Aug. 19 crash occurred just before 7 p.m. as the Cessna was approaching the runway to land.
The helicopter had already landed and exited the runway but was hovering in a nearby field. According to the NTSB, the helicopter crew was conducting a training flight and returning to Carlisle Airport when they became aware of the approaching Cessna.2nd trooper released from hospital; investigation continues into fatal Carlisle aircraft collisionA witness who heard radio transmissions between the aircraft told investigators the helicopter crew instructed the Cessna pilot to "extend his downwind," meaning to continue flying parallel to the runway to create additional spacing between aircraft.
The pilot of the Cessna acknowledged the instruction, the report said. One of the helicopter pilots told investigators the crew received a traffic collision avoidance system alert before spotting the airplane and communicating over the radio. The Cessna pilot had also advised that he was second in line to land. Airport surveillance video reviewed by investigators showed the airplane crossing the runway threshold about 30 seconds after the helicopter crossed it and while the helicopter remained near the airfield.
According to the report, the airplane never touched down. Instead, it continued along the runway before pitching up and beginning to climb.
"After the airplane reached the apex of its climb, about 1 wingspans above the runway, the right wing dropped and the airplane immediately turned right and descended toward the northwest," the NTSB report states. The following four still video images from two of the airport security cameras show the time, locations, orientation of the aircraft and their relative position to each other.
Four still video images from cameras A and C showing the airplane and helicopter as they maneuvered in the vicinity of the runway. Investigators said the helicopter was hovering about 50 feet north of the runway when the airplane leveled its wings, rapidly pitched up and struck the rear section of the helicopter, hitting the tail rotor and main rotor blades.
The NTSB said only about eight seconds elapsed between the time the helicopter exited the runway surface and the collision. The helicopter crew told investigators they were unable to see the approaching Cessna before impact because it was behind them.
As a result of the collision, the Cessna broke into four pieces, while the helicopter's rotor and tail blades separated from the aircraft. Federal investigators said that teams have recovered all the debris at the scene, and will soon be analyzing data cards. Both pilots aboard the Pennsylvania State Police helicopter suffered injuries but have been released from the hospital. The NTSB's investigation continues.
